description: Who changed cap into cape? A quiet gold e! Short vowels become long vowels with a silent e, plus the vowel teams ai and oa and four Rule Breakers.

youtube.title: Magic E for Kids! Cap Becomes Cape | Long Vowels for Grade 2 | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Robo's Word Machine changed cap into cape overnight. Who did it? A tiny, quiet, gold e!
Learn how a silent e makes a short vowel say its name (cap, cape; kit, kite; cub, cube), meet the vowel teams ai and oa (rain, boat), and lock up the Rule Breakers: have, give, love and come.
Try at home: write cap, kit, hop, cub and tub on paper strips and fold a little e card over the end.

do.text: Magic E
Good morning, friends! My Word Machine glitched all night.
Yesterday this word said cap.
This morning it says cape!
Kit became kite. Cub became cube. Who changed my words?
Did you see that sparkle? Something small... and quiet.
Hi! I brought words from Short Vowel Island!
Thank you, Frog! Short vowels make short, quick sounds.
Cap! The a is short and quick.
Kit! Short i.
Cub! Short u.
Hop! Short o. Hop, hop, hop!
Pin! Short i again.
Each word has one vowel in the middle.
Here the vowel is short. That's a short vowel.
short vowel
Frog, can you say all five short words again, fast?
Cap, kit, cub, hop, pin!
You remember those from grade one. Nice work, Frog.
Let's watch the machine very closely. Here is cap again.
Look! There it is! A tiny gold e!
Magic e!
Magic E
The little e hopped onto the end. Now it says cape!
But why? The e didn't make a sound. I was listening!
That's its magic. The e stays quiet at the end.
But it helps the vowel say its own name.
Cap has a short a. Cape has a long a.
long vowel
A long vowel says its name. A, cape!
We call it the silent e, or the magic e.
silent e
Wait. So the e is like a quiet helper?
Exactly! It makes no sound, but it changes everything.
Fun fact: e is the most used letter in English writing!
So the busiest letter is also the quietest. Cool.
Let's practise. I say the short word. You say the long one!
Cap...
Cape! Great reading!
Now the e visits every vowel. First, a.
T, a, p. Tap, like a tap on the door.
Tape! The a says its name.
Next, i. K, i, t. Kit.
Kit plus e makes... kit-eh!
No, Robo! The e is quiet. It's kite!
Oops! You're right. Kite! Thanks for fixing me.
P, i, n. Pin.
Pine! Like a pine tree.
B, i, t. Bit.
Bite! Take a bite of an apple.
Now, o. Watch the o change its sound.
H, o, p. Hop.
Hope! I hope you're having fun.
N, o, t. Not.
Note! A note is a little letter.
Now, u. This one is a cub, a baby bear.
C, u, b. Cub.
Cube! A cube has six square faces.
T, u, b. Tub.
Tube! A long round tube.
C, u, t. Cut.
Cute! What a cute bunny.
And e? Pet plus e makes Pete, a name.
That's a rare one. Most magic e words use a, i, o or u.
Chant with us, and tap your finger on every beat!
Tiptoe e, tiptoe e,
you don't talk, but the vowel sings to me!
Cap... cape!
Kit... kite!
Tiptoe e, tiptoe e,
you don't talk, but the vowel sings to me!
Hop... hope!
Cub... cube!
Your turn! Does each word need a magic e?
Here's a kite flying high. Is it kit, or kite?
Kit, kite. Kite needs the e!
A green cube. Is it cub, or cube?
Cub, cube. Yes, cube needs the e!
A cap on your head. Cap, or cape?
Cap, cape. A hat is a cap. No e this time!
Frog jumps up and down. Is that hop, or hope?
Hop! No e. I just hop!
A long soft coat for after a bath. Rob, or robe?
Rob, robe. A robe needs the e!
A tiny sewing pin. Pin, or pine?
Pin, pine. A sewing pin has no e. Short i!
Wow, you're magic e experts!
The magic e has cousins. They're called vowel teams.
vowel team
A vowel team is two vowels together in one word.
Two vowels walk side by side and make a long sound.
R, a, i, n.
The a and the i team up. Rain!
The a i team says its long sound, A.
Train has the same team. Train!
B, o, a, t.
The o and the a team up. Boat!
Soap has the o a team too. Soap!
So vowel teams often make a long sound, just like magic e.
Fun fact: long ago, people said the e at the end of name.
Over hundreds of years, that e went quiet.
Challenge time! Some words break the magic e rule.
H, a, v, e. The rule says hayv. But we say have!
Rule Breaker! Into the jail you go!
Give. The rule says guyv. But we say give!
Rule Breaker! Jail!
Love has a short sound too. Not lohv. Love!
Into the jail!
Come. Can you hear it? Is it a long o?
No! We say come. Another Rule Breaker!
Have, give, love, come. Four famous Rule Breakers.
have, give, love, come
Most words follow the rule. A few famous ones break it.
We just learn the Rule Breakers by heart. Easy.
Quiz time! Question one. Add an e to tub. What word?
Tube!
Question two. Which word has a long vowel? Hop or hope?
Hope! The silent e makes the o say its name.
Question three. Why does cape say a long a?
The silent e at the end makes the a say its name.
Question four. A sewing pin. Is the word pin or pine?
Pin! No e, so the i is short.
Question five. Which vowel team is in boat?
O a! The o and the a team up.
And our quiet friend? Take a bow, magic e!
Case closed, detectives!
Tiptoe e, tiptoe e, you don't talk, but you help me!
Look for magic e words on signs at home. Bye!
